sections.h2: Your options for selling in Goodyear
sections.html:
A Goodyear homeowner has three ways out. List on the open market, sell without an agent, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes the property in its present condition. Cash usually closes sooner, since repairs, showings and a buyer's loan approval drop out. A listing can bring a higher price when the house is in good order and the calendar is open.

  • Open-market listing: a recently updated house in a master-planned community with an active homeowners association.
  • Cash, as-is: deferred maintenance, a vacant property, or an inherited home the heirs want to close out.
  • Sale by owner: owners who already know the local price range and can manage the paperwork.

Goodyear is one of the fastest-growing places in the Phoenix area, about 17 miles west of downtown. The population reached 125,359 on July 1, 2025, up 30.4% from 96,141 in April 2020, and the city covers 191 square miles. Owners hold 77.7% of occupied homes. The median owner-occupied home is worth $471,300, median gross rent is $1,956, and the city counts 38,188 households of 2.68 people.

So many Goodyear homes sit inside planned communities that an HOA often limits what a seller can do. The city's code compliance page makes the point that some neighborhood rules, parking limits for one, come from private covenants enforced by an association instead of city code.

sections.h2: City code rules to check before listing
sections.html:
Code Compliance responds to complaints about anything visible from the public right of way, so walk the front and sides of the house the way a neighbor or inspector would. Cases usually take 30 to 45 days to resolve, and a notice typically allows 10 to 30 days to fix a violation. The division answers at 623-882-7815 or codecompliance@goodyearaz.gov.

TopicLimit
Weeds and grass on residential lotsUnder six inches, and not hanging over a sidewalk
Recreational vehicles, boats and trailersGarage, or paved side or rear yard behind a solid six foot fence, no more than two
Household petsNo more than four per property
FencesThree feet in the front yard, six feet in the rear; under six feet generally needs no building permit
Trash and recycling containersOut of view of the street except on collection days

The city notes that violations on vacant and foreclosed homes can take months or longer to resolve because owners are hard to locate. If a Goodyear house sits empty, keep the yard cleared and a mailing address on file with the county so notices reach you.

Goodyear's homeowner guidance says all plan submittals and inspections must follow the adopted building codes, amendments and ordinances, including sound mitigation. Permitted work has to stay exposed until it is inspected. Ask the city whether past projects on the house, such as a pool, patio cover or addition, have a closed permit.

Minor jobs, such as a residential pool or spa built from approved standard plans, go through the EZ Permit lane and are reviewed within five business days. Larger jobs, an addition or a detached accessory structure for example, follow the residential submittal guides on the Development Resources page. Call the Building Safety Division at 623-932-3004 or write buildingsafety@goodyearaz.gov. Your HOA covenants are a separate matter, and the city says the owner, not the city, is responsible for knowing them before any modification.

An owner who rents out a Goodyear house must register it with the Maricopa County Assessor under A.R.S. 33-1902. The city says failing to register carries a mandatory civil penalty of $1,000 plus $100 for each additional month. Article 11-1-21, the Residential Rental Property Ordinance, sets minimum health and safety standards for the interior and exterior of any apartment, single-family home or mobile home rented for a fee.

Short stays have their own program. The Finance Department licenses short-term rentals, with application requirements, listing requirements, annual renewal and an emergency and complaint contact record that owners keep current. Its desk is at 1900 N Civic Square, reachable at str@goodyearaz.gov or 623-882-7887 option 4. A.R.S. 9-500.39 keeps a city from banning short-term rentals, though licensing, zoning and safety rules are allowed.

Maricopa County collects Goodyear property tax in two halves, October 1 and March 1. Delinquency begins after 5:00 p.m. on November 1 for the first half and on May 1 for the second, under A.R.S. 42-18052, with a weekend November 1 moving to the next business day. Ask your escrow officer what remains unpaid and how the year will be split at closing.

  • The Assessor's Notice of Value arrives between January 1 and March 1, and a petition is due 60 days after the mailing date.
  • The Assessor must answer by August 15, and the State Board of Equalization hears the next level.
  • Taxes follow the limited property value, which can rise by only 5% a year barring new construction or a change of use, and only the full cash value can be appealed.

The Maricopa County Recorder files the deed. Its office will not advise on legal documents and points customers to a title company or attorney. A completed affidavit of value goes with the deed unless an exemption from A.R.S. 11-1134, such as a gift deed, is written on its face.

sections.h2: What a cash sale skips in Goodyear
sections.html:
With a cash buyer, the lender is gone. Nobody needs an appraisal, nobody orders repairs as a loan condition, and you skip the weeks of showings a listing needs. Escrow and title still run the closing, so your liens, tax split and deed work the same way as in any sale.

Before you accept an offer, fix the cheap exterior problems from the code list above, collect any permit records, and get your HOA contact and payment status in one place. If the house is vacant, confirm the county has a mailing address for you. Compare offers by what you would actually keep after closing costs, and read the agreement before you sign.

faqs.q: Can the city of Goodyear fine me for yard or storage violations before I sell?
faqs.a: Yes. Code Compliance can issue a notice and, if the problem continues, a civil citation that is a summons to appear in court, where a fine can be imposed. Typical correction periods run from 10 to 30 days, and the city can be reached at 623-882-7815.

Yes, with a city license. The Finance Department runs the licensing program, owners keep emergency and complaint contacts on file, and state law bars cities from prohibiting short-term rentals. Licensing questions go to str@goodyearaz.gov.

faqs.q: How many pets and recreational vehicles can I keep at a Goodyear house?
faqs.a: Goodyear limits households to four pets, and it lets a property store no more than two recreational vehicles, trailers or boats in the side or rear yard, on a paved surface behind a solid six foot fence.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a fence in Goodyear?
faqs.a: Generally not for fences under six feet, but exceptions can apply. Front yard fences may reach three feet and rear yard fences six feet. Call the Development Counter at 623-932-3004 before building.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due on a Goodyear home?
faqs.a: Half is due October 1 and half is due March 1. The first half turns delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1 and the second after 5:00 p.m. on May 1, with a weekend November 1 moving to the next business day.
